title: Addressing function error bound
statement: Let $m$ be a nonnegative integer. Encode an input as an address in $\{-1,1\}^m$ together with one sign-valued data bit for each of the $2^m$ addresses, and let $A_m$ return the data bit at the encoded address. For a set $J$ of coordinates among these $m+2^m$ input coordinates, let $g:\{-1,1\}^{m+2^m}\to\{-1,1\}$ depend only on coordinates in $J$. Under the uniform input distribution, the probability that the coordinate selected by the address is outside $J$ is at most twice the fraction of inputs on which $A_m$ and $g$ disagree.
hypotheses_covered: $J$ is a finite set of coordinates among the $m+2^m$ input coordinates
$g$ is a Boolean function on the sign cube
caveat: The formal addressing construction uses specific finite equivalences to encode address and data coordinates; the informal description treats these as the usual address-and-data encoding.
